utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam, and good afternoon to you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Oric. You may be seated and good afternoon to you. Mr. Wubben, appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning -- good afternoon, Your Honours, and also good afternoon to my learned colleagues of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with co-counsel, Mr. Gramsci di Fazio, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink. And later on, Ms. Joanne Richardson will complete the team, as well as acting case manager, Ms. Sanja Bokulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Wubben, and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Madam Vidovic, and good afternoon to you and your team. Shall we bring in the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a very short submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It's for the record. It's regarding the list of issues regarding the interview of witness Dudley to be organised tomorrow morning. I touched base with Defence and provided Defence -- and provided Defence with the opportunity after the interview that will have taken place on an informal basis, with a list of issues of which the US government believe that there should be no problem anticipated in requesting authorisation for use during cross. There might be some more issues in which the request is not foreseeable as to be given no problem. The manner in which the informal list of issues will be communicated to the Defence will be agreed upon by parties, and a decision-making regarding authorisation will be facilitated by the Prosecution in order to achieve an expeditious decision-making as soon as possible, or in the field to provide this information towards the Defence to facilitate their proofing. This offer had been accepted by my colleague, Mr. John Jones, and I appreciate that acceptance. And I consider this as a good step in establishing good relationship between parties. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Because reading the transcript and listening to you, I'm not quite sure whether I am 100 per cent fine-tuned with what -- with you and with what you say the Defence has agreed. But if the Defence has agreed, come to an agreement with you, I am happy and I am sure that my two colleagues will be happy with whatever you have agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm, Your Honour, that there is an understanding or agreement that we will be provided with an informal list of issues before it's been authorised by the USG, and that as soon as possible thereafter, once the USG has approved the list, that that will be provided. So that's my understanding and we are happy -- really, we are happy with any arrangement whereby we have the list before we start proofing. That's the matter of timing which is key for us. But I can confirm that understanding. I would just make a couple of observations. First I would urge the Prosecution to adopt your recommendation, Your Honour's recommendation, that the interview be tape-recorded. I know it's not arguably not a requirement, but I would urge the Prosecution to consider that. I would also note that the interview will be governed by the Rules, and if Rule 68 material emerges, that that would be disclosable. And we above all hope that we won't discover during the course of proofing that the witness feels in any way constrained, that he cannot have complete free and full communication with us. If as a result of this interview the witness feels in any way constrained that he can't say certain things to us because of the interview by the Prosecution, that will pose an enormous problem, and it's a matter I referred to before, and I sincerely hope that that won't pose a problem because we can have no secrets between us and our witnesses. And then just on two separate matters. We filed our reply on Rule 68, the further Rule 68 matter today. It's not an urgent matter but just to let you know we filed that reply, and I believe electronic copy has been distributed. And thirdly, regarding Your Honour's decision on Rule 92 bis and Mr. Paris, the whole object from our point of view of submitting a Rule 92 bis statement was to save time. In light of that decision, we would still have to call Mr. Paris here, we would still have to proof him if he's going to be cross-examined, and in our view in fact we wouldn't save any significant amount of time. In light of that, we want to withdraw that statement. We are going to reconsider whether there is some way we can have an edited or redacted version, but certainly our position now is that that we are not going to call Mr. Paris, and therefore the statement which has been admitted would no longer be so, as I understand it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's, of course, you're entitled to that choice. As regards the rest, I don't wish to say anything else in addition to what we stated yesterday, except that once one of you, this time the Prosecution, has selected a particular way in which to seek to obtain information, this time by seeking to interview the Defence witness a few days initially but before he's supposed to be proofed by the Defence and before he starts giving evidence, instead of following the indication that we had given way back in our September 29th, everyone will have to live with the consequences of his or her actions. Mr. Jones, that's our position. If as a result of this we will have a cataclysm, let there be a cataclysm, that's it. And then everyone will answer for his actions. Yes, the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: While the witness is being brought in, Your Honours, last night I made some comments to you regarding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was thinking of you last night, Mr. Di Fazio. I said while I am trying to relax, Mr. Di Fazio's probably working.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, that was right. But in any event, I made those comments without thinking of all the pressures that both Defence and Prosecution are under, particularly for next week. So I retract everything that I said then. I'll proceed as normally. I won't be seeking any special indulgence, and I'll try and get my cross-examination done as swiftly as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm very appreciative of that, Mr. Di Fazio. You've always been very cooperative. Incidentally, all things going as planned, and of course I have to liaise a bit with my secretary and the rest of my staff, my intention is to have you come together round the table with us this coming Wednesday after we finish the sitting. We'll have a short tete-a-tete, and then I invite you to a Christmas drink before we continue with the last witness and finish off for the Christmas recess. All right? I will come back with more information, more precise information later on. But anticipate, try to leave Wednesday after the sitting free, as much as you can, please. Particularly, you know, I mean, particularly you two and Mr. Wubben and to Mr. Di Fazio and I don't know, the rest of the team, all right? I thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Smajlovic, good afternoon to you, Mr. Smajlovic and welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to finish with --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You know, my optimism took the upper hand. We are going to continue - not finish - with your testimony today. We hope to be able to finish tomorrow. And so I suggest you make yourself comfortable, you're still testifying under oath or pursuant to the solemn declaration that you entered the first day you arrived here. So let's let Ms. Vidovic proceed with her examination-in-chief. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Smajlovic.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your yesterday's testimony, you told us that at one point your wife reached the Oka warehouse in Kravica where the UN Dutch soldier, where she saw her brother, whereupon she was taken back. Can you tell us where was she in fact taken?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was taken back to Potocari to the battery factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us for how long did your wife remain in Potocari in the area of Srebrenica afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a month.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, did she inquire after her brother and her family in general but especially regarding her brother whom she saw at Oka?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did she talk to?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She spoke to a doctor, a Serb, who had been hired from Bratunac by the UN forces in order to assist her and her child. She asked him what was going to be the fate of the people in Kravica among whom she saw her brother. His answer was, "I don't know. You shouldn't be asking too much. You could get killed too." The following day, the same doctor came to see her. She asked him the same question. He answered, appalled that the situation over there was horrible, that chaos prevailed. She inquired what was going to happen. His answer was, "I can't tell you really. There is chaos there. There's hundreds of men there who were massacred, and are to be found in front of the cooperative there."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whilst talking to her, did the doctor pledges anyone?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He mentioned the name of Nikola Popovic, also known as Sojka [phoen], and said that he was spear-heading the killing there, that he was full of anger because he thought that the Muslims had killed his father in the village of Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to be shown a document. This is a document by the command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade dated 5 July 1993 addressed to the command of the Drina Corps, sending the information on the fighters killed, then families of fighters killed. This is quite a voluminous document, Your Honour. We will only refer to relevant pages. The ERN number is 04544200.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the name contained in the list under number 35. Kostadin Popovic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Kostadin Popovic born in 1947, killed on the 7th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, it says 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. I misspoke. Therefore, the 7th of January 1993. Does this date conform with the date of the death your wife heard of as that of Nikola Popovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be assigned a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 985. So this document will become Defence Exhibit D985.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we just enter a correction into the transcript? My question that I put to the witness was not interpreted correctly. My question was: Does the evidence contained in this document correspond to the fact that your wife had heard about the death of Nikola or, rather, Nikola Popovic's father, Kostadin? And that's when the witness answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness? Is this how you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's how we had understood it in any case. Okay. Thank you, let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will turn to a different area now. At the beginning of your testimony, you told us that in the period of May of 1992 was the time when the Muslim population was massacred, raped and expelled from eastern Bosnia. You also told us that after the Serbs had torched large areas of Srebrenica, they abandoned it and that in mid-May or thereabouts, the Muslims started returning to Srebrenica. You told us that you were in fact among them. Later on you'll tell us the exact date of your return but this is my question for you now: Tell us, did the majority of Muslim intellectuals and highly educated people leave Srebrenica or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned some Muslim villages around Srebrenica. Is it true or not that in the course of May and June of 1992, Srebrenica was isolated from most of the surrounding Muslim villages, especially those to the east of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed it was isolated because the Serb villages were placed between Srebrenica and the neighbouring Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which Serb villages divided Srebrenica from the eastern Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The villages of Pribicevac, Spat, Brezani, Srpska Jasenova, Podravanje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the villages you're mentioning are Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Serb villages that were positioned between Srebrenica and Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber which large Muslim villages were located to the east of Srebrenica and which, in the period of May and June, at least until the end of June, were isolated from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Skenderovici, Stozersko, Brezevica, Mocevici, Dedici, Potocari, Osmace, Osata [phoen], Karacici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe we had quite a number of witnesses pointing these settlements to us on the map. I don't see the need, but if you do, the witness can point these for us on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were the following these -- were these villages in touch, one with another at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were isolated, such as Mocevici, Podkorjen, Dedici, because the Serb army set up ambushes in the area and they were unable to move to and fro between the villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber how Srebrenica and its surrounding villages had organised its defence in the period?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They organised themselves locally. In each specific area, there was a group with its leader defending their village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, who chose group leaders?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people locally, from the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understood you to mean that you were in Srebrenica at the time. What was the way the defence functioned there? Who was over there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town of Srebrenica, there were three groups. There was Hakija Meholjic, with about 150 strong group; Akif Ustic with about 50 to 60 men; and I, I was at Kazani with a group of about 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your group in Kazani for which you said had some 30 men, who did it comprise? Were they inhabitants of Kazani or some other men as well?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My group comprised people from Kazani --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the second locality?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And some other refugees who happened to be over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your house?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in my house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Vidovic. Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Could the witness indicate on the map where we have Kazani? Because I can't find it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Otherwise -- anyway, the map should perhaps be in front of the witness throughout his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would suggest that the map is in front of the witness throughout the entire testimony because we might have to refer to it from time to time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, there is a little mistake in the transcript, line 16, it says 1350 I think he said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes,.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And also I don't I think the transcript picked up one other place where the -- where the fighters came in from to join the Kazani group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll ask him that, or perhaps he's heard your remark now and he will come up with an explanation himself. Let's start with marking or indicating on the map the location of Kazani, please, Mr. Smajlovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is already marked. It's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to thank my learned colleague Di Fazio. His answers were not recorded well, as far as the strength of these groups is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many men Hakija Meholjic's group had?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 350 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Akif Ustic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 50 to 60 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness Hakija Meholjic's 150, not 350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact, you know, I mean, in the transcript initially it showed 1350. Now I heard 350. And two days ago or a day ago, when he was describing how angry they were that Hakija Meholjic had not accepted to go and help, he said even though he had 150 men in his group. So is it 150? Certainly not 1350. Is it 150 or 350? I'm not blaming you, I'm blaming the transcript. All we need is the correct figure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, 150 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you very much. And you wanted to know, Mr. Di Fazio where they came from or where they had --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, of course, it's pertinent to the locality issue, and if they are coming in from other areas or other places then I would just like to know where from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: One was missed, just one, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Vidovic. I'm giving you the floor soon. I just wanted to check that I am interpreting Mr. Di Fazio correctly. Exactly. He asked -- he inquired whether the witness could give the information as to where the fighters came in from to join the Kazani group. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just want to end this topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Akif Ustic had some 50 to 60 men; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you talked about your group, you said that it had 30 fighters and you explained where they were from. Since this was not fully entered into the transcript, could you please tell us where the men who were in your group came from?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men who were with me in my group were from Kazani, Kutlici, which is a hamlet of Kazani, and some of them were refugees who found a refuge in Kazani.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kutlici is the second place, K-u-t-l-i-c-i. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Does that satisfy you, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you show the Trial Chamber where Kutlici is on the map, please, and can you please underline?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that you had far more men over there but you didn't have enough weapons?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. We had quite a few men or, rather, many more men than we had arms for them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which other groups you knew existed in May 1992 in the area of Srebrenica, in the join area and in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there was a group at Suceska. It was Zulfo Tursunovic's group. There was Naser Oric's group in Potocari; Mirzet Halilovic's at Pale; Sidik Ademovic's at Susnjari; Hamdija Fejzic's at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat? And, please, Madam Vidovic and the witness, break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you said at Susnjari, Sidik Ademovic, and Bajramovici?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hamdija Fejzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please make a pause before you answer because we are producing difficulties for the interpreters who cannot follow. If you can just make a pause after my question. Is it true that around the 20th of May, 1992 that was the period during which the population of Vlasenica and Skelani in -- particularly was expelled and the period in which Srebrenica was under great pressure with a view to being cleansed?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally hear of the meeting at Bajramovici?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber where Bajramovici is located in relation to your home?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not far from my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you come to know about the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was called by Sefket Djozic and the meeting took place in his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, tell the Trial Chamber who was present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting was attended by Zulfo Tursunovic, Naser Oric, Sefket Djozic, myself, Akif Ustic, and Zulfo Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Hamdija Fejzic there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there other people there, common folk in addition to the ones you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were people from neighbourhood. The entire neighbourhood was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether some other people from Srebrenica itself and its environs were invited to the meeting but did not show up?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Others such as Hakija Meholjic, Sidik Ademovic, and other group leaders were invited but did not show up because they felt the meeting was illegal, not having been called by any legitimate authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what the subject of discussion at the meeting was?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Right at the start, we started to lament about the situation in general, about the situation in the villages where we were, and which we defended. Our conclusion was that we had to lend a hand to each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the result of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The upshot of the meeting was to elect a body which would try to coordinate the different leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why was such a decision taken?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a group was to enter into clashes with the Serbs, in order to prevent that the other villages came under threat as well, the decision was that we should be in touch and constantly coordinate what we do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any mention of who was to head the body at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The body was to be headed by Naser Oric and his deputy was supposed to be Akif Ustic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the decision-making procedure discussed?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By vote.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the Trial Chamber, does this mean that Naser, who was elected to preside the body, does it mean that he himself was unable to take any decisions?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was not able to take any decisions on his own or too decide on any important matters. It all had to be put to a vote.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did that entail? Did it entail for the people to meet and then decide on certain matters by putting them to a vote?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether anybody made any special comments about Naser being elected head?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was said that he was only the first among the equals, that he was not able to take any decisions on his own, and that the decisions were solely to be taken by vote.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the 20th of May onwards, up until the demilitarisation, was this the way in which the things in fact worked?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps all the way through to the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the meeting in Bajramovici, was a specific venue designated as the place where the meetings would always be held?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No venue, and no specific dates were decided upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you have some military expertise that you gained through -- during the war and after. Can you tell us how you perceive Oric's role was at the time? You also had first-hand opportunity to observe that.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His role was to be a coordinator in case difficult situations arose on the ground, to be a coordinator for the different leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that he was supposed to be a coordinator in difficult situations that arose between the different leaders. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please illustrate this for the Trial Chamber by giving us an example? Why was this necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, that's not what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact, to be honest with you, I have taken the -- we have taken the policy of not stopping leading questions, but if there was ever one, this was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. His role was to be coordinator in case difficult situations arose on the ground. Now, that's crystal clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, if it's a question of interpretation of course --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this was misinterpretation. Quite clear. And I just wanted to save time and I merely reiterated what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is the -- what was the question properly interpreted?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it was not properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's the answer that's the important part, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but I want also to know because I --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if Your Honours please, you know why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I told you, Mr. Di Fazio, I was actually saying nothing but I was surprised you were not on your feet even before that. So what was the correct interpretation of Madam Vidovic's question as put in Serbo-Croat? What we have here is: "You said that he was supposed to be a coordinator in difficult situations that arose between the different leaders. Is that what you said?" Yes. That was the question. And then he said: "Yes," and then: "Can you please illustrate this for the Trial Chamber by giving us an example." And then, of course, Mr. Di Fazio stood up with his objection. So what -- The answer was not what we have here in the transcript as having been said by Mrs. Vidovic. The answer was his role was to be a coordinator in case difficult situations arose on the ground, to be a coordinator for the different leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's right. I don't exclude both possibilities, both possibilities may apply and I've got no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't understand the Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no, I understand, Your Honour. What I'm saying is I have no problem with Madam Vidovic leading evidence of both types of situations being coordinated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but one does not follow from the other. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, but one does not follow from the other, and the first answer was very, very clear, and I'll proceed on my cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- on that basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is extremely unfair the way Mr. Di Fazio is proceeding, because it's been made very clear that this is a problem of interpretation and my learned counsel has been struggling -- has been struggling to get a word in and, of course, she is a few seconds behind with the interpretation and has been unable to make that point. Mr. Di Fazio is saying I'm going to take the answer, the misinterpreted answer, for the purposes of my cross-examination. Well, if he does that we are going to request the tape, we will get the tape, we will get the correct interpretation, and you'll see that the witness gave the answer which my colleague said. So rather than trying to confuse everyone and everything, why don't we actually proceed on the basis that there have been a misinterpretation until we discover that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's what I have been asking all along. We want the correct interpretation of what the witness had stated and what Madam Vidovic stated as being his reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can we get the tapes then because it's essential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course. Let's get a replay of the tape. At that point we are talking of page -- it's 14, we can start from 14.56.13. You said that you had some -- and while we are listening, hearing the replay, please everyone stay silent so that the interpreters can listen in carefully. So, please, I beg you to cooperate with us. Technically to be able to do that now takes a long time. So the suggestion is that we come back to this after the break and we continue with the evidence now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's fine by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it fine with you, Madam Vidovic? All right. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the role of Naser Oric the way you understood it at the time? Could you please answer that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The way I saw it, his role was to coordinate among the leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber why -- can you perhaps give an example why it was necessary for somebody to coordinate things among the leaders at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can give an example. Hakija Meholjic could never see eye to eye or cooperate with Akif Ustic. The same thing went for Hakija Meholjic who was unable to reach an agreement with Zulfo Tursunovic. That is why somebody was needed or that body was needed to be set up to coordinate things among the leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like the witness to be shown P73, Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By the way, there will be two breaks today, like yesterday. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look first of all at the signatures at the bottom of this document? Can you tell us, do you -- can you recognise Naser Oric's signature?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know his signature because before the war when we worked at the police, he would sign off his reports at the end of his shift. And I would never say that this is indeed his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Are you familiar with the signature of Hamdo Fejzic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, while we worked at Tenergoinvest [phoen] together, he worked with me and his signature was much shorter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have given a very clear answer about Oric's signature, and again this has not been recorded. It's not in the record. But I don't want to ask you a leading question. Can you please repeat what you said about Oric's signature?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I worked with Naser in the police before the war and that he signed his reports at the end of his shift. And I would never say that this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at the contents of the document? If you can look at the name listed under number 7, this document refers to Bajramovici, and it says here Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Srebrenica TO Staff 1/92, Bajramovici, 20th of May, 1992, decision, and at the end you have this number 7. Please, Ahmo Tihic, was he present at the meeting in Bajramovici where you were present?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was his name mentioned at all at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not mentioned at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know him from before the war?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had known Ahmo Tihic before the war, and the first time I met him in mid-August because I spoke to him about what had happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that he had been wandering around the villages and that he had been with the people fleeing from those villages in the woods around the place, and that he was sorely disappointed with what had been happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Muslim people in the villages around that area accept him at all?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the words next to the name of Bogilovic, Becir, from Srebrenica: "An outstanding activist in armed resistance against the aggressor in the area of Suceska." Did you know Becir Bogilovic well?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I worked with him together in the police before the war. He was never an activist. He was just a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you about this document. Apart from the group leaders that were present at the meeting in Bajramovici, were there any other groups in the Srebrenica area that were fighting against the Serbs, that were not present there, nor had they been invited to attend the meeting, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were such groups. They could not be invited to the meeting. That was the Jiljeskovik [phoen], the Poznanovici, the Osata group, the Gladovici group, the Ostrika group, the Karacici group, the Osmace group, and the groups that I had already mentioned. The groups that were flee -- that had fled Tokoljaci and Trubari.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about Mocevici, Brezovica, Poznanovici, Dedici, Podkorjen, Imici [phoen], Busmulici [phoen]? Do you know whether any of them had been invited to attend the meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I've already mentioned the -- that the groups that I have mentioned, Dedici group, Podkorjen, Mocevici, Brezovica, Skenderovici, and Storasice [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the meeting in Bajramovici, was there any talk at all or any decisions were taken about those groups of people?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What had been agreed in Bajramovici, did that also bound -- bind them?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It did not bind them. It bound only the groups that were present or, rather, the group leaders that were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from those groups from the villages around Srebrenica, were there any other groups of armed Muslims in the Bratunac area or in the fringe areas of Srebrenica and Bratunac who were fighting the Serbs there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were groups in Bljeceva, Glogova, a group in Voljavica, in Zaluzje, in Biljaca, in Zanjevo, in Abdulici, in Jagodnja, in Joseva, and in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me clarify this. When you say Atolici [phoen], Zanjevo, are you referring to the fact that they were positioned there or are you referring to the people who had fled the -- those villages?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. They were in large groups of refugees. They were not positioned in those two villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, Madam Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I have a question to you. If this -- these villages are important to be named, I think it would be necessary that you are not so quick because on the -- in our transcript, we do not have any names of villages. So either the villages are not important or you should make sure that they are really named at least in your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But they will fill them up later when they go through the transcript, Judge Eser. But if she wants to go through them now again, if you think that that is very important, we can -- I think we can go ahead and then this matter will be looked up later when they go through the transcript. Usually they do. All right. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may be done at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because Judge Eser prefers to have the complete list now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You don't have to repeat it now. It's more for the future. You're naming the villages so quickly that it's completely impossible to follow on the map, and if it is important that we get an idea what's going on there we should be able to read them, to recognise them. But if they are not important, then leave them. Either/or.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please slowly go through the villages? I asked you about the groups. In addition to the groups from the Srebrenica villages, were there any other groups of armed Muslims in the Bratunac area or in the fringe areas of Srebrenica and Bratunac where they fought with Serbs against Serbs and you went through them. Can you please now, this is a very appropriate remark made by the Judge, could you please slowly enumerate the names of those villages, so just repeat them once again, the groups?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bljeceva, Glogova, Konjevic Polje, Voljavica, Zaluzje, Biljaca, Zanjevo, Abdulici, Joseva and Jagodnja.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any groups in the Srebrenica area of armed men from Vlasenica or elements of the Muslim population in the fringe areas of the Vlasenica municipality who also were fighting against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were the group of Becir Mekanic, the group of Fadil Turkovic, and the groups in Cerska and the villages around it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you mentioned Glogova, is there any other village where the people of Glogova had some connections with it and can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Bljeceva.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does Bljeceva have a hamlet?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Those groups from Vlasenica that you just mentioned and the groups from the Bratunac municipality, did they have any -- anything to do with the agreement reached at Bajramovici?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not have anything to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now let us go back to the document of the 20th of May, 1992. If you look at the document, you will see here that it says the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Territorial Defence Staff Srebrenica. This body that was elected at that time in Bajramovici, was that in reality the Territorial Defence staff or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like the usher to show to the witness Defence Exhibit D272, and I would like you to keep the document dated the 20th of May, 1992. This is a document from the Supreme Command staff, temporary formation, municipal staff of the defence, municipal defence staff with headquarter support unit. I wanted to ask you whether you're familiar with the term provisional establishment?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the preparatory stage I showed you this document and that you had a very thorough look at it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what is the purpose of the provisional establishment?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Provisional establishment is a document stipulating the organisation of a certain unit at war -- during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please go to page 7 of this document. That would be page 10 in the English version. This is a chart, the chart. You can see here it says municipal defence staff organisation chart, types 1, 2 and 3. Do you agree, first of all, that you saw that this provisional establishment referred to 1992? That's what you saw at the start?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that according to this chart, the municipal defence staff needs to have a commander, the Chief of Staff, assistant for IPD and religious matters, a security organ, assistant for logistics, financial assistant? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that according to this document, the staff needs to have an anti-sabotage unit, an engineer corps, technical service, transport and traffic service and other services; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, that body set up in Bajramovici, did it establish a staff along these lines or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that body a staff of this kind comprising all those units listed here and everything else that is envisaged in this establishment?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not the way this is supposed to -- it is supposed to be according to this establishment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did it look anything like it at all?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It didn't look anything like that at all. The structure of the people who attended the meeting, those people did not have any military knowledge, and we didn't even think about -- we couldn't even dream about setting up something like this because in the situation that we faced, it was impossible to do anything. The conditions simply did not exist for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss at all staff in the military sense of the term or any other bodies of that kind at that meeting on the 20th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No it was not discussed at any moment at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Bajramovici, did you talk about the police, military or civilian?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not discuss the civilian police or the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can remove the document. And now I would like you to go back to the document P73. If you can have a look, the statement of reasons somewhere down the middle it says: "Owing to an urgent need to merge self-organised armed groups into larger units, and establish a single command of armed forces in the struggle against further enemy aggression, and unite the movement for the liberation of occupied territories of Srebrenica municipality, a single military command of armed groups shall be formed under the name of the Srebrenica Territorial Defence staff." I'm asking you, you attended the meeting and you were present in Srebrenica up until the time when it was demilitarised. Is it correct that at that time, or at any other time up to the demilitarisation, the units really were unified and whether single military command was ever established, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The units were never unified and the single command was never established throughout the time all the groups operated locally in those areas, and they were called Hakija's group, Suad's group, Mujo's group, Hazim's group and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At any time up until the demilitarisation, did you have the equipment to establish the staff, the means to establish the staff?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not have any equipment or means to establish the staff because you can see from this document what you need in order for the staff to function.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the communications equipment?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not have the communications equipment. We did not have the barracks. We did not have the equipment. We did not have the uniforms, weapons, ranks, insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document can be removed now. And I would now like the witness to have a look in parallel to two Defence exhibits, D626 and D627.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those documents, D626 is a certificate concerning Naser Oric, father's name Dzemal, that he attended a course for trainee police officers, and the second one is the request for a job application for Naser Oric and I would like you to look at both those documents. Do you agree that under his education in both case, it says that he has a police officer course, that he's a graduate of a police officer course?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you knew Naser Oric. From what you know -- first of all, tell us, how old was he in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, have a better look, Witness.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no, 23, going on 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not referring to the document. I'm just asking you, at the outset of the war in 1992, I'm asking you if you know how old Naser was old [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, how old was -- he was? 24, 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From what you know, at that time, when the war started, and when this body in Bajramovici was established, did he have any military knowledge as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not have any military knowledge from what I knew, and on the basis of our conversations while we worked together I knew that he had attended a police officer course and that he attended the specialist course for body-guard and escort duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he did his national service, and do you know whether he held any rank at that time when he was doing his national service?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that he was a lance corporal.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know in what arm of service he was?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was in the nuclear, biological and chemical defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if he had any military knowledge regarding the command and control?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm sure he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did Naser Oric appear in Srebrenica from what you know? When did you see him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- at the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what he had been doing before that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was a police officer serving in Belgrade, in Pristina, and that that's where he worked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that he appeared towards the end of 1991. Did he gather the Muslim youth around him? Was he a popular person among the young people?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was not popular. At that time, he was the personal escort of Slobodan Milosevic. Milosevic was a symbol of Serbdom and we would see him quite often on TV. He was standing right beside Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Oric's father?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was he doing in 1990 and 1991? Well, in fact, up until the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naser's father was a car mechanic, top car mechanic. He had his own private repair shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If somebody claimed that Oric had his car fixed in a car mechanic shop owned by a Serb in Bjelovac, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't be correct. Because when Naser came to Srebrenica in late 1991, he drove in a new Renault 5 car and at that time his father was the authorised -- had the authorised garage for that type of a car. So he would never take his car to some other mechanic to fix the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If somebody were to say that at that time Oric -- so I'm talking about the period from the end of 1991 or in the course of 1991 up until the beginning of the war, that he gathered the Muslim youth of Srebrenica around him, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can now remove those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to play a video, Your Honours. That's 2844. And now I would like you to listen to the conversation very closely, and I would like to ask the interpreters not to follow what is written in the transcript but to listen carefully to the parts of conversation that we are playing here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This part of the video recording pertains to the events of the 20th of May and now I would like you to play the video from 002253 to 000320.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Unidentified Speaker: Before you continue on with the story, I want to ask you about the [unintelligible] very briefly [unintelligible] that meeting occurred on the 20th of May 1992, would that be correct?"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, first of all I wish to ask you whether you know anyone seen on this footage?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, do you agree that the following question was put by the person seated on the right-hand side here, on the monitor? First of all, I want to ask you whether you listened to this video material in my presence several times?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the person seated to the right is the one putting questions? And before we continue with the story, there are just a couple of things that I would just like to briefly ask you about this meeting. We have information that the meeting was held on the 20th May, 1992; is that correct? Is it correct that the -- this is the question that was put? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please continue playing the tape and please listen closely. Let's play the tape from 000320 up until 340.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "That meeting occurred on the 20th of May -- information I think about a meeting at the HQ. That was before."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you hear Naser answering, "No, not the meeting then. That's the information I mean -- I mean when the meeting of the staff took place, that was before, we hadn't arrived by then. We hadn't arrived by then?" Was that the answer that you hear him say?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the meeting that the Prosecutor in his question claimed to have taken place on the 20th of May, that Naser responds to that that the meeting was not held then, on the 20th of May, but, rather, that they had not arrived by then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to refer you to transcript 3 of this video footage, which is page 1 in the English version, where the question -- the answer was not interpreted correctly because to the question concerning the meeting on the 20th of May, Naser Oric answered, "No, no." Here, the entire answer by Naser Oric was left out, where he says, "We had not arrived yet. By then." I also wish to draw to a series of confusions and discrepancies that exist between the B/C/S and the English version because in the English version apparently the question is put by Carl Koenig [phoen], whereas the B/C/S version has the initials ST. This isn't the reason why I'm showing the witness this transcript. I have a different reason for doing so. I just wanted this to be stated for the transcript. I wish to continue further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Like the Defence, if Your Honours, please, the Prosecution is also concerned about discussions of evidence in front of witnesses, and this is the sort of matter that's best reserved for another occasion. I have no problem with Madam Vidovic putting the transcript to the witness, of course. That's most proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I fully agree with you, Mr. Di Fazio. Let's proceed. Please avoid any discussions in the presence of the witness. And one other thing about this exhibit and the other one where -- the interviews with -- the alleged interviews with the accused, these, as you can imagine, I mean both Prosecution and Defence, these are of absolute importance, and if they are, it's equally absolutely paramount -- of paramount importance that we get the correct translation or interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Particularly on this issue. Particularly on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's very important, it's very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'll make sure that this particular segment is given particular attention to, raised with translation services, or we will resubmit it and make sure that the -- it's correctly translated. And I heard what the English was too. And I understand the point that Madam Vidovic is making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please try to understand our concern is -- goes a little bit further than what you have just stated. What we are inviting you to do is to make sure -- and this invitation is being made now because we've got very little time left, Mr. Di Fazio. Make sure that this tape and the other one, the whole entire interview is reviewed and that the translation/interpretation is agreed to by both parties, and if there is disagreement on any particular part, that we may be made privy to it so that if it is necessary for us to intervene to make sure that we have the right interpretation or translation, if one of you contests it, then we will be able to do so in good time. In a timely fashion, in other words. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond, Your Honour, why I decided to take this course? Every time I have a witness, I, of course, wish to place this marker just for the record. However, in this case, the matter is far more serious than catches the eye, especially of the OTP's. The matter at hand is also the translations by -- of the documents handed in by the Prosecution concerning Oric. Especially when we have a witness seated here who is aware of these matters, who knows whether the meeting took place before or after, then it is necessary to have the response from the witness, because Oric himself hears that the interpretation is wrong. That is why I wanted this to be entered into the record, the reason why I wanted the witness to see this. Can we continue playing the tape? From 001950 up until 002050.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Do you understand that? Yes. I just wanted -- one or two short questions I wanted to ask you about some of the things we said yesterday. As I understand it, we now are getting to the 20th of May, 1992, and that meeting at Bajramovici. One thing I'm not sure of, and maybe you can clarify it for me, the re-entry into Srebrenica, did that occur before or after that meeting? No, no. No, I mean after or before? The entry into Srebrenica took place after this meeting. In the --"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you confirm hearing the Prosecutor repeating the question concerning the 20th of May, 1992 and the meeting that took place on that day and the question is put to Oric?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Prosecutor asked Oric whether the re-entry to Srebrenica took place before the meeting at Bajramovici and that Oric decisively answered no?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In saying no, did he explain that the re-entry to Srebrenica took place after the meeting at Bajramovici?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what Naser confirmed, that this was not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I want to ask you. You were at Bajramovici. You attended the meeting at Bajramovici. When did the Srebrenica residents in fact return to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people from Srebrenica returned to Srebrenica after Goran Zekic's death, not before. On the 9th of May, 1992, Hakija Meholjic and Akif Ustic were already there and many people were already there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there with my group from Kazani.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does Oric provide accurate information here?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he does not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you something else. You heard the Serbo-Croat or Bosnian language used by this interpreter. What is your opinion thereof?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpreter interpreting at this meeting is not that familiar with the Serbo-Croat language. He seems to be guessing, because the terms "ulaz" [phoen] and "ulazak" [phoen] in B/C/S are two different terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at document P75 now. This is purported to be the document of the Srebrenica Territorial Defence staff dated 26 May 1992, whereby the TO Srebrenica -- TO staff Srebrenica is expanded to include Atif Krdzic, Nedzad Bektic and Senaid Tabakovic. Look at the document, Witness, and please look at the name of Atif Krdzic. Is this man from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He does not hail from Srebrenica. He is from Osmace, and lives in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nedzad Bektic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, I mean, on computer monitor, we are still see seeing this still from the video and not the document that is on the ELMO, if this could be corrected, please. Okay. Thank you. Just for the record to give the opportunity to whoever is following to know which document we are talking about basically. I thank the technicians and we may proceed. Thank you, Ms. Vidovic for being patient.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next to Nedzad Bektic's name, the text reads: "Organiser of armed resistance against aggressor in the region of Kragljivoda." Do you have any comment about this?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nedzad Bektic come to Karacici, and he has nothing to do with Kragljivoda because there was a different leader.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the allegations in this document, are they true?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the name of the actual group leader in Kragljivoda because this is not in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sefik Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or, rather, Your Honour, if this is an appropriate time for a break, I can stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank so much, Madam Vidovic. We'll have -- how are you doing for time, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm doing my best to end today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we have one minute. If you want to go back and listen to that part of the tape, I understand it's ready. Do you want to listen to it now before we go to the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. No, we listen to it in the original language, in B/C/S. I mean -- and then it's translated to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Q: Did anybody make any specific comments about Naser's position. A: Yes. I do remember it was said that Naser was only the first among the equals and that he was not able to decide about anything on his own, but that exclusively it had to be done by vote. Q: From that date, from the 20th May onwards, through to the demilitarisation, was this how in fact the matters functioned in reality? A: Yes, perhaps even through to the end of the war. Q: At this meeting at Bajramovici, was a specific venue agreed upon where the body was to meet, a headquarters? A: No. Neither a place nor the time. Q: You explained to us that you have some military expertise, that you even gained after the war. Looking back at these events, how do you see Oric's role at the time and you also had the occasion to observe it? A: Oric's role there was only to be a coordinator in difficult situations arising on the ground, amongst the leaders."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And then her question, Madam Vidovic's question, which is what you contested.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, that confirms the correct translation. That was the correct translation. He said difficult situation and surely that resolves the very issue which was in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, I think it's a mixture of both. It's a mixture of both. He was a coordinator of difficult situations on the ground amongst the leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely not, Your Honour. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will not allow any further discussions on this in the presence of the witness. Let's have the break now. It will be of 25 minutes, just to be on the safe side. Madam Vidovic and Mr. Wubben, would you be agreeable to that? And the rest? All right. 25 minutes starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm waiting for the accused. I want to make sure that he is here. May I suggest that you forget about what we've heard and more or less now we know what the witness said in any case, and we move ahead. Mr. Di Fazio particularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I'm perfectly happy with what I've heard. My quick query is answered. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic. Let's move ahead with the next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to let you know that in the course of this session, my colleague will unfortunately have to absent himself from the courtroom to attend to an urgent matter and we will continue outside his presence until tomorrow. I will move on with my questions now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I trust the urgent matter is not the reception at the Japanese embassy which I'm going to miss because I'm sitting here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly not, Your Honour. I'd like the witness to be shown D4.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, P4.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is allegedly a document by the Srebrenica TO staff dated 15 June 1992. Is it true, Witness, that I've shown you this document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document and specifically at the name under 4, TO Osmace, Atif Krdzic, or, rather, I will quote the document: "With the aim of confronting the aggressor and engaging in the struggle for liberation, all the local leaders of self-organised armed groups are ordered to immediately commence developing the organisation and establishment of the Srebrenica TO units," in particular the date here is 15th of June. My question has to do with number 4, TO -- Osmace TO, the name is Atif Krdzic. Is it true that Atif Krdzic was at the head of the group in Osmace at any point in time throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. Mirsad Dudic was the group leader there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that the Nedzad Bektic did not lead the Kragljivoda group.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us again whether on the 15th of June, 1992 Ahmo Tihic had any contacts with Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We -- he did not have any contacts with Srebrenica, nor did we have any contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the person under number 9, Luka TO, Mustafa Durakovic? Have you ever heard the name? Do you know the man?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never heard this name before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of Luka?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have. I know that Ikan Mujic was the group leader there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I wish to refer you now to the part which says: "Services attached to the Srebrenica TO, war hospital." On the 15th of June, 1992 and in the subsequent period up until August 1992, was the war hospital set up in that period, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. The building that was called hospital was razed to the ground basically after the Serbs had left Srebrenica. There was nothing. There were just the walls standing. There was no equipment. There was no furniture, no fittings. The roof itself was dismantled and taken in the direction of Skelani. The hospital itself was located in my house and that's where the wounded and the ill were taken at the time. Avdo Hasanovic, medical doctor from Suceska, came over to look at the people and assist them as far as he could.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The building you were referring to, as far as you know, when was it made operational? When was it made serviceable?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was partially made operational only at the end of July, when people of their own accord started going from house to house collecting whatever they could, sheets, blankets, mattresses, to make it look like a hospital, although it was not a proper hospital even then.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it anything like a proper hospital throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. During the war, we took desks from offices and the school building, and it was on these very desks that the people were operated on. People were -- their wounds were dressed and then they had to lie on these desks, and they were nothing like beds, and these were wounded people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Minor point, no objection. Is the witness talking about his house here or some other structure?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it so, but I stand to be corrected if he's not, of course. But that's how I understood him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's just not clear. I mean, I would think the Defence would want it to be clear, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you can ask the witness to explain whether he is still talking about his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, is it true that the hospital up until the end of July 1992 was in fact located in your own home?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my own home.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then you went on to explain that the hospital or, rather, the building that you said was called the hospital was made operational?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness mentioned this yesterday. I think we are wasting time on this. I'm doing my best to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. Judge Eser, yes .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I'm just not clear, the witness talked about that the building had been torn down. And where was this building located, in which part of Srebrenica?
