utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the entrance into the town of Srebrenica. That was Baratova, the neighbourhood of Baratova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: A building on the other side of the street?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can ask him direct whether it was in the proximity, whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Was it in the proximity of the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this the billing we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, across the street from the PTT building. It was not torn to the ground. It was just simply totally devastated. Everything had been taken away from it. Just the walls were left standing. The entire -- all the fixtures and fittings had been taken away, but the building itself still stood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The translation we have had perhaps has not been the same. It looked as if the whole building had been destroyed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour, because the witness did clarify the matter. This is probably due to the speed, the rate of speed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No matter how much in a hurry we are, please leave some time before you start your answer. Here is says the platoon of the military police will be set up by Mirzet Halilovic. In June 1992, as far as you know, was the military police set up in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when it was set up?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 1st of July, when the War Presidency was elected. It was in the village of Bajramovici in Hamdija Fejzic's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber whether you were present at that meeting on the 1st of July, 1992 and what happened there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was present there. That meeting was convened by some prominent people from Srebrenica and the people who were the mainstays of the SDA party. I went to that meeting because I had been invited by Zulfo Salihovic, a neighbour of mine. He was one of the main figures in the SDA at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any special reason why you would remember the 1st of July, 1992? And is there anything about that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do. Resid Efendic, who was my colleague from the police, he was a police inspector, he used to be a police inspector before the war, he also attended that meeting, and at that meeting he nominated me as the commander of the military police, and then most of the people there did not agree, and they said, since Mirzet Halilovic is an expert in martial arts, and he holds a black belt in -- a karate black belt, they thought he would be a much better person for that job.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to this -- the previous document. Is it true, then, that the military police was set up on the orders of the body that had been established in Bajramovici on Oric's order, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police was established pursuant to a decision issued by the Presidency, not the decision by Naser Oric, nor had Naser Oric anything to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now go back to -- I will in fact be asking you some more questions about this meeting, the meeting of the 1st of July, 1992 where you said that the War Presidency was elected. Can you please tell us who was the main person at that meeting? Who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. Those were the representatives and, in fact, the main figures in the SDA party: Hajrudin Avdic, Zulfo Salihovic, Hamdija Fejzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did they say? Why was it necessary to establish the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that meeting, they said the things that we actually knew at that time. In the town of Srebrenica itself, the -- there was a huge influx of refugees from the areas that had been taken by the Serb military. Those refugees did not have any accommodation, and then they started breaking and entering into apartments and homes of the people from Srebrenica who had fled into the woods as parts of those large groups of refugees and who had not yet returned to their homes. There were also quite a few civilians who carried weapons. They were totally out of any control. They were carrying weapons around the town. And they agreed that some order should be restored to Srebrenica itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now let me show you a new document. Its number is 1839572 A and it is dated 1st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before the witness has a look at this document, there is a mistake here. It says Dudic, Dudic Hajrudin, whereas in the English -- in the original it says, Avdic, Hajrudin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, have you seen this document before, together with me?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that at the top of this document, by way of a title, it says, "Send the decision for appointment." You attended the meeting on the 1st of July, 1992. Do you have any idea why this title is here in this form?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The names that are listed here, I remember that quite well, Hamdija Fejzic explained that they cannot appoint themselves but that the decision on the appointment needs to be issued by the War Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was located in Sarajevo for this body to be legal.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at those names here. It says Hajrudin Avdic, Hamdija Fejzic, Dzemal Becirevic, Resid Efendic, Naser Oric, Jusuf Halilovic, Becir Bogilovic, and then deputies, Azir Zekic, Mirsad Dudic, Sefik Mandzic, and then below there is a line, military police commander, Mirzet Halilovic. Do you agree whether in fact those people were in fact appointed to those posts on that date as it is stated here in the document. Please have a good look at the document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those people were elected. The people that were above the line, elected by the people, and by the prominent persons in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were they appointed to?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were appointed members of the Srebrenica War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the handwriting of -- in this document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This was written by Resid Efendic, who was appointed the technical secretary of the body.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with his handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I explained a while ago, we worked together. He was an inspector in the same police station where I worked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So there is this line here, and do you agree that it is written in the same hand, military police commander, Mirzet Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document reflect the actual situation, what was happening at the meeting of the War Presidency, the fact that the -- that Mirzet Halilovic was appointed the military police commander?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the people elected those people here into the War Presidency, they sat down and they elected the military police commander. So the body that I'm talking about the is the War Presidency of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any discussion at the meeting about how the military police was to function, whether independently, as part of those armed groups, as part of the Public Security Service? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember. It was said that the military police would be working hand in hand with the civilian police and that their chief would be Becir Bogilovic. Their premises where they were supposed to be housed were the premises of the public security station, so both the military and the civilian police would share the same premises in order for Becir Bogilovic to be able to exercise control over the work of both police forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The last thing that you say, was that one of the conclusions reached at that meeting on the 1st of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the conclusion reached at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like this document to get a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Vidovic. And thank you for also pointing out the mistake at the top and first name. This document will now become Defence Exhibit D986.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was an agreement reached at that meeting for -- in fact, let me rephrase: What was agreed regarding the War Presidency at that meeting, what it should or should not be?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I did not quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it agreed what place in the government the War Presidency would have, what role it would play?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was said that as of that time on, the War Presidency would be the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the witness to be shown document P254. This is an order from the War Presidency dated the 14th of October, 1992. We have the signatures of the SJB chief, Becir Bogilovic, on one side, and Hajrudin Avdic on the other side. And let me quote: "Anyone in possession of a firearm, ammunition, explosives, communications equipment and medical supplies must immediately report it to the commander of the nearest unit or military or civilian police for verification and utilisation thereof."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, you told us that at the session that you attended yourself on the 1st of July, 1992, when the War Presidency was established, that the issue of people carrying arms without any control was discussed. Do you remember what was concluded? Was anything concluded?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The conclusion was that all the weapons that were not controlled should be seized, but that both the military and the civilian police should take part in this effort.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree whether a specific person was specifically tasked with this?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the chief of the civilian police, Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Bogilovic at the same time the chief of the military police?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Becir Bogilovic was the chief of both the civilian and the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document in fact reflect what was agreed immediately after the establishment of the War Presidency, that the weapons should be seized?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask the usher to show the witness document Defence Exhibit D5. P5. This is purported to be an order of the Territorial Defence staff of Srebrenica dated 29th of October, 1992. It says here: "The military police is hereby ordered in accordance with order number 92/92 to carry out an investigation in Krusev Do and place the seized weapons at the disposal of the Srebrenica armed forces." First of all, do you agree that this purported order is referring to an order of the War Presidency number 91/92?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me quote from this document some more. "According to available sources the following persons are in illegal possession of weapons." And then we have names of three people, Zijad Mandzic, all of them are from Krusev Do. First of all, please tell the Chamber where Krusev Do is. Is it near Srebrenica at all? And if you have that map and if it is on the map at all, you could perhaps point it out.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it is on the map, I will point it out. Krusev Do is about 80 kilometres away from Srebrenica. So that would mean that Krusev Do is closer to Zepa. It's about ten kilometres away from Zepa. It's closer to Zepa than to Srebrenica. And Krusev Do and Luka were never part of the Srebrenica enclave. That's one thing. Secondly, it would be illogical to dispatch anyone, because I've said a little while ago that there were Serbian ambushes on the territory and Serb positions, and now to send somebody to that place to get a rifle, that would make no sense. Third, Luka and Krusev Do, up until the demilitarisation, had been under intense artillery and infantry attacks from the direction of Han Pijesak and Milici throughout the time. So that this order is illogical. What is written here is just not logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you think that this order contains accurate information, that the contents are logical and accurate?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The contents are not logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will ask you if you can just point Krusev Do here.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't see Krusev Do here. It's somewhere here in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it's not on this map?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've told us that it's a -- how far away from Srebrenica is it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 80 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now ask you something else. When it comes to Becir Bogilovic, do you have any knowledge of the fact that he was wounded at one point in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 2nd of July, 1992, at Likari, and he was replaced by Nurija Jusufovic in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the usher to show a new document to the witness. It's numbers 03592911. The name here is the SJB commander Srebrenica, Nurija Jusufovic. And let me just point something out to you, Your Honours. We have an error in the English translation. It should say citizens from Karno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Vidovic. That's pretty much obvious. So there shouldn't be any questions from the Prosecution. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me quote: "Avdic: The citizens of Serb ethnic background from Karno are detained at my place, there are nine of them. They had been brought in last night during the night and now they are at my place. Please find a solution for us, what to do with those citizens." And my question to you in this regard is: When the SJB chief was -- Becir Bogilovic was appointed, and Mirzet Halilovic as the chief of the military police, was there any discussion at the meeting who they should report to?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mirzet Halilovic was supposed to submit his report to Becir Bogilovic, and Becir Bogilovic to Hajrudin Avdic, the president of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document mentions Nurija Jusufovic and the SJB Srebrenica. Was that the man that you said replaced Bogilovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This man by the name of Avdic, who would that be in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be Hajrudin Avdic, the president of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like this document to get an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And that will be Defence Exhibit number D987, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like the witness to be shown Prosecution Exhibit P590. The document has a title, it's written in Cyrillic, military police, copies. That's what it says. And then on the relevant page, it says, "Armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, military police station, Srebrenica, the list of the military police staff." And I would like you to look at this document. Did you go through this document in detail with me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document counts 47 names. The first one is Mirzet Halilovic, and now I would like to ask you about some people on this list. Do you know the person listed under 11 here, Damir Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a fighter in my group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the person listed under 28, Ibrahim Kancetovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was also a fighter in my group and he didn't have anything to do with the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 32, Ahmir Jahic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was in my group, a fighter. He did not have anything to do with the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about Damir Salihovic? Did he have anything to do with the military police?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he had nothing to do with the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your group, up until the demilitarisation, so from the beginning of the war until the demilitarisation, did you have any military police officers?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A group that counts about 30 people is not a formation. It's not a unit for it to have military police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were these people in 1992, particularly in that period, July 1992, linked in any way with Mirzet Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not have any links with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to have a look at the person listed under number 22, who would that be, if you say it says Ikan Mujic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ikan Mujic. He was the leader of the Luka group. This was the man who never left Luka up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to you have a look at the name listed under number 34, Fahrudin Ahlic, born in 1966. Please, do you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my colleague, a police officer, who was the group leader in Brezovica, and later on, he became the member of the extended War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have anything to do with Mirzet Halilovic or the military police?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Neither with Mirzet Halilovic nor with the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about number 46, Senad Golubovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Senad Golubovic, as of the 1st of July, when Mirzet went to become the military police commander, he was the leader of the group at Pale up until the day he died.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please look -- you can go over to the next page and look at the name listed under 61, Sead Ademovic. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was also a reserve police officer who worked with me. He was the brother of Sidik Ademovic, the leader of the Susnjari group. He never had anything to do with the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the basis of what you saw here, does this document contain accurate information?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It does not contain accurate information, and this document lists some people who had never even come to Srebrenica at all up until the demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you perhaps mention some names?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zijad Jakubovic and some other lads that I know on this list.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In reality, on the basis of what you know, how many people were in the military police in the summer and autumn of 1992? Could you please tell the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a small group, they did not have any weapons. They wore civilian clothes. They did not have any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question pertaining to this. As far as you know, from the beginning of the war, until the demilitarisation and in fact up until the end of the war, did Naser Oric ever have any body-guards or escorts?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't need one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to play a video recording, that is Prosecution Exhibit P329, tape runs from 292092. I would like the tape to be played from 013250 to 3406.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And please listen carefully, Witness. You did listen to this carefully with me, did you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please play the tape from 013250 to 013406.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Invention should you have known that this was going on? "What do you mean how am I supposed to know? "Was it military police who were in charge of the prison? "Of course. This was the duty of the head of the military police, what the military police were doing there. This was also the duty of Hamid Salihovic, who was carrying out the interrogation of these prisoners, and I had much bigger problems elsewhere, protecting villages from Chetnik attacks and from Chetnik breakthroughs."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, based on what you've heard here, do you agree that in answering the question as to whether the military police officers had kept a prison, Naser Oric did not reply with either a "yes" or an "of course"?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in answering the question put by the Prosecutor, Naser literally said, "Commander of the military police, I don't know what that is -- what that's about, what the military police officers were doing. I mean military police officers." Is that exactly what was said in our language?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, witness, did you hear Oric saying in his reply, "The commander of the military police was charged with that, and Hamed Salihovic to conduct interviews with these prisoners"?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that at no point in time did Naser say that this was also Hamed Salihovic's duty who interviewed or interrogated these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in our language, the following has a completely different meaning? Was charged with holding interviews, and held interviews?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you hear Naser say, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment because I'm sure it makes sense in Serbo-Croat but as it is, it doesn't make sense in English. How are we going to make the distinction? You say "Do you agree that in our language the following has a completely different meaning, 'was charged with holding interviews' and 'held interviews.'" In English obviously the two things are completely different but I don't know which expression in your own language you meant to refer the witness to. At least we can have an indication of that, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. My question was --.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did I make myself understood?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, you have. You've made yourself clear. I only call on the interpreters to follow me. My question was as follows: Do you agree that in our language, it is quite different to say "was charged with holding interviews" and "held interviews"?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which way this was interpreted, but when you say "held interviews" this is something that was in the past and it was done, do you agree with me.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the transcript of this interview reads, the text, as was translated into English because the transcript says that Hamed Salihovic held interviews, which means that he was holding them, that he interviewed these people and, of course, there is a great difference to that. It's quite a different matter if you're charged with doing something and if you in fact do that. This was the essence of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Madam Vidovic and I hope that this is another matter that you will look into, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We will examine it minutely, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we continue playing the footage and namely from 013406 up until 013427.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "A question that those [unintelligible]. Is the military police a branch of the military under which -- of which you were the commander? "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that the question put by the person seated to the left was translated to Oric as follows: "Is the military police part of the military structure?" And the -- Oric immediately answered "yes"?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that after that, Oric was interpreted the following question: "Under which you were commander"?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How would you understand this question to mean, had it been put to you, "under which you were commander"?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is definitely an illogical question, "Under which." What does this mean? This question put to him made no sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, the way the question was interpreted to Oric, do you agree with me that the very fact that the question was cut into two parts means that the question put to him was general?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how I understood it to mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you understand this Prosecutor's question?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked him whether the military police was under the military structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a general question or --

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was general.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we play the tape further, Your Honour, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would rather have it played back a little bit so that I hear it again first. Because I'm getting a little bit confused here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's play just this last segment and then we can proceed. I just want to rehear it, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "There is no question that those were big problems. Is the military police a branch of the military, under which -- of which you were the commander? "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We can go ahead. But I could hear, at least in the English part, in the English interpretation part, that it's -- indeed the gentleman on the left did say, "under" but immediately then went on to say "of which". First he said "under" and then he said "of which" you're a commander. Let's proceed because this would become an argument and I want to avoid arguments. This is testimony basically. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Would you have expected there to have been the type of inquiry that you had into the one death for these other deaths if there had been deaths in custody?"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, first of all, the way the question was put, is it understandable in our language?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point hear the interpreter interpreting to Oric the part, "if there were deaths in the" -- "in prison" -- "in the prison"? Did you ever hear the interpreter mentioning the word "prison"?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The words "prison" or "death" were never mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to play another clip of this footage and I would like then the witness to leave the courtroom. Can we continue, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Let's proceed with the video. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "If -- if I had found out that there had been such cases, then we would have started an investigation. And in fact we did start an investigation [unintelligible] other such cases. So to give you a concrete example, with Envir Halilovic, which happened after this."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You said you'd like the witness to leave the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First I would like to put a question to the witness in connection with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have heard Oric's answer. Do you agree with me that Oric literally said the following: "If I found out about something of the sort happening, either I or the War Presidency would, of course, initiate," and so on? Do you agree that Oric had clearly stated "War Presidency" just as he said investigation?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He clearly said "I or the War Presidency."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the witness to leave the courtroom for two minutes only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I don't think there will be time for him to have a coffee, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Jones, that we are to expect no further problems with regard to Major Dudley -- or, not major, sorry, Lieutenant Colonel Dudley? Has he arrived?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's what I'm about to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, if there are any problems envisaged, do alert us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I certainly will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and I appreciate that. And good evening to you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the sake of the record I wish to state the following: As you had occasion to see, and my learned colleagues from the OTP do have a person there speaking Bosnian and can ascertain that easily, the words "War Presidency" were left out here. The interview is swirming [phoen] with cases such as these that I have illustrated here and I -- we will file an application in connection with this. But I wish to state the following: At the first Status Conference, when we were assigned this case and when I received this interview, I read it, I compared the Bosnian and English versions in the presence of the Chamber's legal officer, I drew their attention to these errors in the interpretation and I asked them to remedy them. This has, however, not been done. The case at hand is not merely to correct a misinterpretation, but indeed, in many situations, Oric himself received wrong interpretation, and we believe that this is something we should draw your attention to and we will submit a very detailed filing in connection with this. I think the witness can return now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much Madam Vidovic for this information because, as you know, I came to the picture in this trial just before it started, and I don't even think I had one Status Conference. I had the Pre-Trial Conference. But once you have mentioned this, I'm going to give instructions to my staff to go back through the documentation relating to the status conference and I'll try to find out what is in the record there. Yes. I recognise Mr. Wubben, and then Judge Eser has asked for the floor. Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, as I recall, as I came also later than Madam Vidovic in the -- in this case, but what I recall there had been an instructions to our CLSS to make a complete new and -- new review with a view to a translation of the interviews, and that has been done, that process, and I invite in that field to the Trial Chamber to also take a look at that process as well, and the evaluation afterwards. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear. Perhaps you can give me an answer. I'm not quite clear of the role in which the witness was asked here. Was he a sort of expert to say that it was incorrect way in which the translation occurred or was performed or was it that he should confirm whether what has been said in the interview was reality? Could you explain what the role was of asking the witness these questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do that gladly, Your Honour. The initial parts had to do with the meeting at Bajramovici and the witness had direct knowledge of the time when the meeting at Bajramovici was held, about what Oric said there, and what the discrepancy between what the witness was saying and what Oric was saying consisted in. This is something he also commented on. And in the part that had to do with the organisation of the military police, I asked him about that part and it was only in passing that I showed the witness these inaccuracies. The purpose of the witness's presence here was not that of an expert but, rather, that of a participant in all these events that we talked about, and it was in passing that I wanted to draw Your Honour's attention to the fact that these errors exist. All the time, the Prosecutor has been using individual, isolated sentences from this interview, and use it against our client. We have a right to confront the witness with this, and to do it by simply showing him these matters just as the Prosecutor did, extracting single sentences and confronting witnesses with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I didn't want to deny any right of you to ask. I just wanted to know the purpose of this exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you, Judge Eser. I'm sure no one doubted that either, from the other side. But as I understand it to be, and I want to make myself clear on this, is basically, Ms. Vidovic has been using this witness to show once more to us that the transcript or the translation into English of what is being said in Serbo-Croat in reality during the interview is not reliable, that it contains a lot of mistakes and errors. And I take what Mr. Wubben has stated, that they have gone through all this again. I was told two days ago by one of my staff that we would be handed the new -- that you had some problems with the CD, with the DVD, incidentally and that we were expecting it one day and that it wasn't ready and we were going to have it the day after. Has it been handed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Not yet, Your Honour, but I'm happy to do it by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not mentioning this to make you run.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, no. I'm glad you asked, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It just came back to my mind and I just wanted it make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It's ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Ms. Vidovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please. Just one -- I don't want to embark on any further submissions. I do say this, though. Insofar as this particular interview was concerned, accuracy is, of course, important and -- it's supremely important. These issues arise from time to time, and before we finally put to you what the full, complete situation is with respect to moves that are being made to enhance accuracy, check accuracy, look at accuracy, on the part of the Prosecution, I need to go back to the correspondence, and I need to speak to my case manager and get more details. These issues arise. You can't deal with them in this environment, so can we revisit it briefly, and I'll give you a full and better report at some later --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely. Please do not take it for a moment that I am suggesting that this matter has now been sufficiently debated and closed. Far from it. I think it hasn't even started, to be honest with you. I just hinted sometime back what the legal position is, namely that this is your document, and therefore you have got the full onus of proving the reliability and probative value of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Defence hasn't got any onus to prove anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And we understand and agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So at the end of the day, please don't put us in a position where something which is considered in any procedural setup as the queen -- we call it in my country, the queen of evidence. I mean, when you have a statement by the accused himself, that's how we refer to it, but if that becomes unreliable because there is not only a suspicion but a continuing indication that the translation is unreliable, I mean, you can imagine what --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand. I understand all of these issues, and Madam Vidovic is quite within her rights to highlight anything that she feels needs to be highlighted. All I was saying is that insofar as the background is concerned, can we revisit at a later stage when I'm fully -- of all of the surrounding issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely. I thank you for that as well, Mr. Di Fazio. And ourselves will also check what happened during the Status Conference. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I only wish to assist. I raised this matter at the first conference, that was the first 65 ter conference, after my client was indicted. That was at the first 65 ter conference in the -- during the pre-trial stage, and then I raised this matter repeatedly later on. But I would now wish to continue with my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Bring the witness back, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Smajlovic, we are in a position to continue now. We needed to discuss something which didn't concern you, but since it was a submission we needed to discuss it in your absence because no submissions should be made in the presence of a witness. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in this last recording you heard, did you hear the name of Hamed Salihovic mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally know Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him. Hamed Salihovic was my chief in the police. He was the chief of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the war, that's to say from the beginning of the war through to the demilitarisation, did you have any contacts with him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, at a certain point in time, was Hamed Salihovic a member of a body in charge of security matters?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know until what time he discharged these duties? Did you ever talk to him about it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to him. He discharged these duties until the end of 1992, when he resigned having been already at the time appointed to a different post.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that his name is linked with the subregion or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm familiar with that. He was elected president of the subregion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that capacity, that's to say president -- in the capacity of the president of the Presidency or the president of the subregion, as you put it, as far as you know, from the contacts you had with him, did he have anything to do with security in combination with that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It with not be logical for him to wear two hats at the same time, to do two jobs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he himself confirm to you that he had resigned to his duty in charge of security matters?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will briefly put some questions to you with regard to the subregion. The units from Vlasenica and Bratunac, were they at any time during -- and until the demilitarisation, under the command in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to play another videotape now. This is P328, 2/2, or rather, 2844-722, tape 13, and could we play the tape from 004730 until 004835.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "I have just one thing. Yesterday you asked me if there was a military court. In Srebrenica after Zalazje, a military court was formed, and I found this very -- I found this out yesterday [intelligible] through contacting my fighters after the demonstration outside. I'm not a computer. I cannot remember all of this stuff. They told me -- they told me and I remembered later on that Zulfo Tursunovic was at the military court, as some kind of military judge."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, based on what you know, is it true that at any time during the war, a military court was set up in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A military court was never set up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fact stated here by Naser Oric that the military court was set up after the Zalazje action, is it true?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The information he gave is not true. He did not know at the time what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From what you heard here, is it not completely clear that he came by this information through communications he had with his fighters after the -- yesterday's part of the interview or actually that he did not have this information himself? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agree. And on several occasions, he made contact with me concerning some events and what was happening at Bajramovici, at Zanik, at Peciste. As a police officer, I told him that he should only divulge those stories that he himself knows about or is certain of, and if he is able to, to immediately hire a lawyer who has experience in international humanitarian law to be able to communicate with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Naser Oric have such a lawyer at that time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who his lawyer was?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was Mr. Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a local lawyer from Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A local lawyer from Tuzla, a lawyer that specialised in fraud, not in international humanitarian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, it's a matter of clarification. Do I -- I think what the witness is saying, but it should be clarified, is that on several occasions, Mr. Oric made contact with him concerning some events and what was happening at Bajramovici and then he -- this witness provided him with his advice. In order to understand that evidence, you should know when that was occurring, whether -- I understand it to be occurring during the interview process, but if not, if that's not correct, then I think it should be explicitly made clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you are right in your assessment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you say earlier on: "And on several occasions he made contact with me concerning some events and what was happening at Bajramovici," when did these contacts happen? When was this? When did he contact you on several occasions? Which year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was in 2001, when Naser gave this interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I mean -- I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- the way of understanding, because otherwise this lawyer of -- with international humanitarian law expertise wouldn't fit in anywhere, Mr. Di Fazio. Anyway, let's proceed. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether Oric contacted other people apart from yourself to get the information he needed for the interview? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me now move on to something else. I will now show you two documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will move on to another topic, and I would like the witness immediately to be shown P33 and P76.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one do you start -- do you want to start with first, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P76, Your Honour. P76.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please have a look at Exhibit P76. The Territorial Defence staff Sarajevo signed by Sefer Halilovic. It says: "I appoint the -- Naser Oric as the commander of the Srebrenica municipality TO staff." Could you please comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can. First of all, the format of this document is not proper. For somebody to be appointed to a post, it should say "Order." That should be the title. And then it should say such and such a person is appointed to such and such duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at the other document, that's P33? The last page. In the middle of this document, which is dated the 8th of August, 1992, in the middle of this document, it says, that is listed under R: "To the municipal TO staff, Naser Oric to the establishment post of the commander of the municipal staff." And I want to ask you something. You were one of the commanders of the group in Srebrenica. Did you ever find out about the existence of those two documents, the order about the appointment of officers, stating that Naser Oric was appointed to this post and the same kind of appointment made by Sefer Halilovic? Did you ever know about the existence of those documents from the summer of 1992 until the demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And at that time it was impossible for anything of this sort to be communicated to Srebrenica at all, to be relayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say relayed or communicated, are you aware of the existence of radio ham operators in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else. After the 8th of August, 1992, was the single command for the groups existing in the territory of the municipality of Srebrenica become operational [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It never became operational. As I already said, this was all done locally, at the local level, and in the areas from where the local leaders were originally.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why was it so? Why, after the August, the month of August, 1992, did you not manage to organise, to unify, all those groups?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we did not have the proper conditions. We had some obsolete weapons. In order for all of it to become operational, you would need the barracks, uniforms, ammunition, weapons, communications equipment, logistics, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica itself, how did it function? For instance, I will ask you: Hakija Meholjic, did he ever accept Oric's command?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Hakija just went there to assist when he wanted to do so. He would not take anyone's orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to be given Prosecution Exhibit P80. P80. This is the submission of the information on the formation structure of Srebrenica armed forces. You have first establishment structure, then you have page 2, where it says: "7 TO Srebrenica" and then you have the companies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, I would like to draw your attention to the fact that under the title, first establishment structure, it says on the 20th of May, 1992, the Srebrenica TO staff was formed in Bajramovici from the 17th of April 1992 to mid-October 1992. The first regional units were formed under the names of TO as follows. And then go to the next page, number 7, TO Srebrenica, and I would like your attention to be drawn to the last item here, when you enumerate the units, it says: "The Kazani, Bajramovici platoon, F 22, 20 VO conscripts, commander Suad Smajlovic." Do you agree that if you look up there, that the item number 3 is also Bajramovici company? I wanted to ask you, were you established as a platoon at that time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were an independent group of about 30 men. We did not have anything to do with Bajramovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Below that, it says: "The commander of the TO Srebrenica is Akif Ustic. TO Srebrenica has 803 conscripts." Was Akif Ustic at any point your commander?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. He had his group in Stari Grad, in the old town. And before that, as I said, he was appointed the deputy in that body that was established in Bajramovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the old town, Stari Grad, you see Hazim Omerovic here. Was Omerovic, Hazim, at any point at the head of some kind of a company in Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. He was just a very good friend of Akif Ustic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 2, where it says the second establishment structure. The 3rd of September, 1992, the staff of the armed forces of Srebrenica makes a decision to appoint the operational staff, appointing Osman Osmanovic as its chief. And please go to page 4; the number is 0207584. Please look at number 4. It says Independent Battalion Srebrenica, headquartered in Srebrenica, commander Safet Mujic, five companies, and then below that, as the third company, headquartered in Kazani, commander, Suad Smajlovic. What I want to ask you is, first of all, your group, were you ever part of something that was called the Independent Srebrenica Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. We were always acting on our own accord.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Safet Mujic at any point your superior officer?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that man. I had never met that man during the war and while I was in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the last sentence here, it says: "5th Company based in Srebrenica, commander Hakija Meholjic." I want to ask you there this Safet Mujic was the commander -- whether -- of Hakija Meholjic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That man did not accept anyone's command. He didn't recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are the quotes that I just gave you from this document accurate?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you regarding this document, in 1992, in fact up until the demilitarisation, were there companies, battalions, brigades, established in the military sense of the word in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At no point. Somebody may have written this down on paper but in reality, the picture on the ground was different. There was just those groups on -- armed groups operating independently.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Hakija Meholjic and his men, despite the fact that Hakija did not recognise anyone's command, did they fight against the Serbs at any point?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I just said, when he felt like it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about Akif Ustic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the same thing. He also acted wilfully and that's how in fact he went on this mission and he got killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he accept Oric's command, despite the fact that on paper he was his deputy?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not. He did not take orders from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, the local leaders of those groups, were any of them appointed by Naser Oric, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was always something that was done by the people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when we talk about the geographical location of Potocari, you said that Oric had a group in Potocari. Did Oric's group control the whole of Potocari, geographically speaking?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were other groups that acted independently in Potocari. For instance, the group in Susnjari, Sidik Ademovic in Jadici, in Brezevo Njiva, in Pale, the Budak group, Pestica [phoen], Gogazi [phoen], Duge Polje [phoen]. These are all the groups that were operating independently from each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could Oric have replaced -- removed from office any of the leaders from that area and appoint others?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Did he on one occasion try to remove you from the post?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He received information that I had not gone to Baranovce [phoen]. That was misinformation. I tried to tell him that. He wouldn't listen to me. And in the end I told him, "Let's go to Kazani and then you tell my group that I can no longer be the leader of the group." And when we got to Kazani, I got my group together, and Naser tried to say why, and Medo Hakic [phoen], one of my fighters, got up and he told him, "You go to Potocari and remove from the post whoever you want there in your group. You will not do that here." And they all left, leaving Oric and myself alone. And then he told me, "You made them say that." And I said, "No, because they only trust me and no one else."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This might be a convenient place to make a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if we have a 30-minute break, do you think you will finish, Ms. Vidovic? If not, we will have a 25-minute break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I will be able to complete the examination, and I think we should have a 25-minute break because it gives me an additional assurance if I have the five minutes more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We will have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, go ahead, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, does the name Almaz Hasanovic mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Almaz Hasanovic hailed from Zanjevo. He was sent over to Biljeg to Ahmo's to be the group leader there. Those who were over there made him go back immediately by saying, "You should go back to where you come from, to those who sent you over here in the first place." From there, he proceeded on to the village of Joseva where he was told the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he himself told me as much once he returned from up there, and he spent the whole time in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before I turn to this document, I wish to ask you the following: Who sent him back from Biljeg? Who told him, as you said, to back from where he came from?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahmo did. Ahmo Tihic did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please turn to this document now. Do you agree that you have seen the document before, that I showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the heading. It refers -- or rather draws back to the decree of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In October 1992, in the area of Srebrenica, did you hear of the -- of a decree issued by the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The first time I heard of the decree was when I arrived in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at item 1, which says "Unauthorised movement of fighters from unit to unit is prohibited." Then look at item 2. "I order that by 25 October 1992, constant communication be fully established by couriers and communication means from lower units to higher units and superiors in accordance with the military organisational establishment structure as defined in order number 28/92." Witness, do you agree with me that this is a generic order applicable to all units or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it was applicable to all the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a group leader, did you ever receive this order?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what was going on after the 18th of October, 1992, can you say whether men moved from one group to another of their own free will?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And nobody could bar them from doing it. They went wherever they thought they'd feel better or they'd be better off.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Up until the demilitarisation, has there ever been a communication through couriers that took hold?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that period, was there a communication system introduced from lower to higher units in accordance with the establishment structure, as stated in this document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a system in place of reporting among the groups on the ground?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There never was one. I for one know that I never wrote or submitted any reports to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the period through to the demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the period up to the demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information to the effect that somebody else apart from you ever wrote any reports to Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Never. We lacked paper for rolling up cigarettes, let alone for reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to correct my question. Did you have any information to the effect that somebody else from any other group wrote any reports to Naser Oric? Because it was interpreted as if I suggested that he himself wrote the reports. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't quite understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did any member of any other group ever write any reports to Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why? You were saying?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we lacked paper to roll up cigarettes, let alone to write reports. Q.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness P20. Prosecution Exhibit P20.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is allegedly an authorisation issued by the commander of the armed forces of Srebrenica. Please pay particular attention to the date here, 24 March 1993. It says: "The commander of the Srebrenica armed forces hereby issues authorisation. The Kutlici unit is hereby authorised to mobilise the entire population temporarily housed in Kutlici village and send it to positions. Any person who refuses to obey the order on mobilisation shall be taken into custody at the prison in Srebrenica." Based on what you know, was there a special Kutlici unit in the Srebrenica area or is that the group of men you mentioned as having been with you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no separate or special unit. These were men from my group. In the period mentioned here, or in the period before that, it was quite absurd for anyone to issue or write an authorisation. This was the time of the fiercest battles for the survival of Srebrenica. At that time one expected Srebrenica to fall at any -- any day. Especially the people from Kutlici, Kazani and other places, they all joined fighters who had weapons and they took along axes, hoes, whatever they had, with them to prevent the Chetniks from entering the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The date of the 24th of March, 1993, isn't that the period in which Mladic was with his staff in the period -- in the area of Jadar, the footage we saw, the video clip, isn't that the same time period?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the leader of the group including the men from Kutlici, did you ever see this document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. All the men were with me on the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any need for any such authorisation to be issued?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said it was quite absurd that any one would actually write something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will move to another topic now. Do you know that Srebrenica was demilitarised on the 24th of March -- on the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that an agreement was signed about the demilitarisation of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under this agreement, were the demilitarised zones of Srebrenica areas where any military organs such as the military police or any other units, were they able to be active?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, you, the people in Srebrenica, did you do your best to cooperate well with UN forces?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: With UNPROFOR forces?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How would you yourself estimate the relations between the UNPROFOR force and the Srebrenica population?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were very poor. First of all, UNPROFOR members regarded us as primitives, simpletons, looked down upon us. They placed all the blame on us. They regarded us as savages, the reason why they had to be there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, superior officers of UNPROFOR, did they exert pressure on Naser Oric, his group and other groups, to leave the entire demilitarised area of Srebrenica immediately after the demilitarisation took place? That's to mean to leave physically, not just to surrender arms.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were officers of the United Nations who repeatedly called on Oric to leave the area of Srebrenica as a matter of urgency, together with all the local leaders. On several occasions, Oric spoke to me about this matter, and I told him that I myself did not know what should be done. And I advised him to consult with the authorities in Sarajevo, to see what their opinion about this was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this something that the Sarajevo authorities suggested that he do themselves?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically what the Sarajevo authorities told him, but I know that he himself refused to leave Srebrenica as long as people were there. And if Oric and the other groups left, the people would be left to their own devices.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what you know, did UNPROFOR start sending contradictory information about Naser Oric's conduct towards them and about the conduct of the other groups toward them to the authorities in -- of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, did they have any reasons warranting such conduct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not. I don't know what their purpose in doing this was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what sort of relations did UNPROFOR have with the Serbs? Were you able to observe anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I myself was able to observe this and thousands of other people who were in Srebrenica at the time. It was at this point in time that UN APCs contained Serb officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, if Your Honours please, there is a passage of evidence that in my submission simply doesn't make, with respect, much sense. The question based on what you know did UNPROFOR start sending contradictory information about Mr. Oric's conduct towards them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know where you're heading. Yes, he did -- should be yes, they did, because I noticed your face at the time and how surprised you were. Yes, he did. Should be yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. But also there is no explanation of what "contradictory information" is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. But let's put it like this. You know what our function is. If you want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I won't say any more about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want to ask him on cross-examination, then ask him on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I'll withdraw my comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't fill in blanks. It's neither for you nor the Defence. Yes, Ms. Vidovic. We were -- he had just mentioned that he used to see Serb soldiers in UNPROFOR trucks and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could my learned colleague from the OTP permit me to finish my examination-in-chief? I believe that in this case, as in general, there must have been an error in the interpretation, because I never mentioned the witness contradictory information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, did I not ask you that based on your knowledge, UNPROFOR started sending the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina different information on Oric's misconduct, improper conduct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you have information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question to you was what sort of relations UNPROFOR had with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I omitted to say that -- or rather, I did not say that these were Serbs or -- in a truck but, rather, these were Serb officers in a -- in a UN APC, who passed through Srebrenica, made -- drove all the way -- all the way around Srebrenica and went back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember when this took place?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the demilitarisation of Srebrenica. That's to say, the months of May or June.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did the people in Srebrenica take this?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the people saw these Serb officers, they went in front of the base which was in -- within the compound of a weaving company there at the entrance to Srebrenica area and they protested the fact that the Serb officers were to be seen with the UN members. They were so enraged that they wanted to shatter the vehicles that were parked within and without the compound of the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, in the course of 1995 in particular, did not the UN soldiers under different pretexts attempt to make Oric leave Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will now move to a different topic. I would like the witness to look at three Defence exhibits at once, at one time. These are documents 02621750, 02621517 and 02621437. I will have the same questions in relation to all the three documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at document 02621750. It says the "attack on Zalazje," and please turn to the last page of this document. And then please look at the document entitled "the attack on Jezero" and then have a look at the last page of the document again. And then have a look at the form that is entitled "the attack on Brezani" and, again, I invite to you look at the last page of that document. Do you agree that you had already had been -- had looked at these documents in detail together with me?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is always the last page of the document because it appears that the witness's name appears on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what I'm asking you is: Have you at any point been the source of information for the analysis of combat operations of the Territorial Defence or the Bosnian BH army from 1992 until 1995?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you in any way cooperate on this project, either as a researcher or as a reviewer?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In May 1997, were you at Zivinice, work there, went there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was a member of the 281st Brigade in Dubrave, which was part of the 2nd Corps under the command of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you look at all those documents and do you agree that on all of those documents there is your name, Suad Smajlovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether this is your signature?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to look at the document 02621473 [as interpreted]. That would be the attack -- the form that pertains to the attack on Brezani. Can you please look -- look at the last page again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a mistake in the transcript, it's not 1473, it's 1437.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 37, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document, the last page, where it says -- please look at what it says here, "Commander and signature." Do you -- can you tell the Court what name is this?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Haris Saric [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Haris Saric, was he the commander of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether that man is still in the BH army?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He has been suspended for unknown reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if those documents could be given an exhibit number I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The first one, which starts with ERN 02621750, will now become Defence Exhibit D988. The second one, which starts with ERN 02621437, will become Defence Exhibit D989. And the last one, which starts with ERN 02621517, will become Defence Exhibit D990.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would now like us to move into private session for the next couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means. Let's move into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be resumed on Friday, the 9th day of December, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
